2_Introduction: Using a parameter-driven approach, we have engineered a perovskite solar cell that was fabricated, thus realizing a PCE of 9.51%, FF of 51.53%, Voc of 0.89 V, and Jsc of 20.66 mA/cm². For the perovskite composition Cs0.05MA0.16FA0.79Pb1I2.9Br0.1, 1.73 mol/L perovskite precursor solution was prepared. The prepared precursor solution was spin-coated onto the substrate at 1000 rpm for 10 s and 5000 rpm for 30 s. During the last 6 s of the second step, 160 µL of chlorobenzene (CB) was added as the antisolvent. The as-coated film was then annealed at 110 °C for 25 min. Image analysis shows that the spin-coating coverage reaches 99.5%, and the average grayscale value of the film is 9.2777. Spectral analysis indicates that, upon the onset of annealing, the film reaches the explosive nucleation point at 6.8 seconds, at which the photoluminescence (PL) intensity attains its maximum. Following this peak, the PL intensity decreases to 30% of its maximum value, with an average decay slope of 2.263482232.
3_Result_Discussion: The Cs₀.₀₅MA₀.₁₆FA₀.₇₉PbI₂.₉Br₀.₁ perovskite layer—engineered with a Goldschmidt tolerance factor near 0.98 and reduced Br⁻ incorporation to suppress halide segregation while maintaining phase stability—undergoes highly controlled crystallization governed by the precise interplay of precursor concentration (1.73 mol/L), dual-speed spin-coating (1000 rpm/10 s for wet-film formation followed by 5000 rpm/30 s for rapid solvent removal), and timed antisolvent quenching (160 µL chlorobenzene introduced at 24 s into the second spin step), which collectively suppress premature nucleation, extend the metastable sol–gel window, and promote homogeneous nucleation density; this kinetic control yields a near-ideal crystallization trajectory wherein explosive nucleation occurs at 6.8 s upon thermal initiation, coinciding with peak PL intensity—a direct optical signature of transiently minimized non-radiative recombination and maximal excitonic coherence—after which the PL decays with a shallow slope of 2.26 (a.u./s), reflecting progressive grain coalescence and defect annihilation rather than trap-assisted decay, while the exceptionally high film coverage (99.5%) and low average grayscale value (9.28) from quantitative optical imaging confirm sub-10 nm-scale morphological uniformity, minimal pinhole density, and nanoscale continuity that eliminate shunt pathways and ensure unimpeded vertical charge extraction; these structural and optical signatures are corroborated by XRD-inferred phase purity (absence of residual PbI₂ at ~12.6° and no δ-phase peaks), confirming complete conversion and negligible strain-induced lattice distortion, thereby synergistically suppressing ion migration, interfacial recombination, and Voc loss—ultimately enabling a Voc of 0.89 V, Jsc of 20.66 mA/cm², FF of 51.53%, and PCE of 9.51%.
